newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania sentences four communists to jail.
newsitem.headline: Albania sentences four communists to jail.

text.p: An Albanian court on Monday sentenced four men to a maximum of 2/1/2 years in jail for forming a communist party and conspiring to overthrow the government.
Presiding Judge Gjergji Pojani said Sami Meta, Timoshenko Pekmezi, Kristaq Mosko and Tare Isufi had continued the illegal activity of the communist party in contravention of Albania's constitution.
"The communist party has been outlawed but the defendants have continued its activity in secret," Pojani said.
"Their aim was to take power with violence, overthrow the constitutional order and establish the dictatorship of the proletariat," he added.
Sami Meta, 62, received 2-1/2 years, Timoshenko Pekmezi, 54, two years and Tare Isufi, 73, and Kristaq Mosko, 45 got one year each.
The four, who admitted founding a communist party, said they would appeal against the case brought by the country's secret police.

After the demise of Albania's hardline dictatorship in 1990, the country introduced a series of laws to punish former leaders and prevent a resurgence of communism. Parliament outlawed all communist organisations in July 1992.
